body: @aehlig wdyt? Maybe not show this for repos originating from macros outside of main workspace?

FWIW there are 2 actions you can take for these:

- fix it upstream for everyone
- lock the dep in your own WORKSPACE
Yep agreed with @keith, this has helped me to improve the fetching from upstream rules so I would prefer to keep the error messages as is.

I totally agree that fixing it upstream would be nice, but for that the error should contain more information to make it an easy thing for me. Right now it is not straight forward to locate where it is coming from. If bazel know, please print full context.

>  Right now it is not straight forward to locate where it is coming from. If bazel know, please print full context.

Bazel does know where the rules are defined, but there is the request to not print too much information; so currently, that information is only recorded in the `--experimental_repository_resolved_file`. If there is consensus that we should print that information on the console as well, we could easily do it, the same way as we currently do it for repositories involved in failures.

Please ask yourself what the purpose of the message is. If you want people to fix those things, tell there where to fix it. The easier you make it the easier they will fix it. 
If you don't want people to do anything, remove the message :)

issue.body:
When building rules_k8s with Bazel 0.25.2, I get these messages:

```
DEBUG: Rule 'io_bazel_rules_python' indicated that a canonical reproducible form can be obtained by modifying arguments shallow_since = "1555445174 -0400"
DEBUG: Rule 'io_bazel_rules_jsonnet' indicated that a canonical reproducible form can be obtained by modifying arguments shallow_since = "1556260764 +0200"
DEBUG: Rule 'subpar' indicated that a canonical reproducible form can be obtained by modifying arguments shallow_since = "1551997562 -0500"
```

It's unclear to me what it means, and whether I should care about the messages.

I filed this issue #11040 and bisected the problem.

I appreciate if anyone can confirm that what I'm doing is right or not:

According to the [Google Test tutorial](https://google.github.io/googletest/quickstart-bazel.html), it said to prepare `WORKSPACE`:
```txt
load("@bazel_tools//tools/build_defs/repo:http.bzl", "http_archive")

http_archive(
  name = "com_google_googletest",
  urls = ["https://github.com/google/googletest/archive/609281088cfefc76f9d0ce82e1ff6c30cc3591e5.zip"],
  strip_prefix = "googletest-609281088cfefc76f9d0ce82e1ff6c30cc3591e5",
)
```

This produces:
```txt
INFO: SHA256 (https://github.com/google/googletest/archive/609281088cfefc76f9d0ce82e1ff6c30cc3591e5.zip) = 5cf189eb6847b4f8fc603a3ffff3b0771c08eec7dd4bd961bfd45477dd13eb73

DEBUG: Repository com_google_googletest instantiated at:
  C:/users/XXXX/WORKSPACE:3:13: in <toplevel>
Repository rule http_archive defined at:
  C:/users/XXXX/mrkfkorq/external/bazel_tools/tools/build_defs/repo/http.bzl:336:31: in <toplevel>
```

According to `DEBUG` message, I add `sha256` property in the `WORKSPACE` like:
```txt
load("@bazel_tools//tools/build_defs/repo:http.bzl", "http_archive")

http_archive(
  name = "com_google_googletest",
  urls = ["https://github.com/google/googletest/archive/609281088cfefc76f9d0ce82e1ff6c30cc3591e5.zip"],
  strip_prefix = "googletest-609281088cfefc76f9d0ce82e1ff6c30cc3591e5",
  sha256 = "5cf189eb6847b4f8fc603a3ffff3b0771c08eec7dd4bd961bfd45477dd13eb73",
)
```

To do this, "a canonical reproducible form can be obtained by modifying arguments sha256 = ..." messages dissapeared.

I'm also appreciated if I could have the pointer to clear this problem's cause and how-to fix in the Bazel manual.
@ryohji that's correct. Adding the sha256 will ensure that you get the same version each tiem the build runs.
